findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify how the verdict_obtainable rule handles gate_ops.completion_reconcile pre-populating result['criteria'] from raw_criteria before reconcile_verdict runs — key the fault on the MODEL's emitted criteria/findings (or capture the emptiness before line 295) rather than the post-injection result['criteria'].
evidence: Step 2: 'when a non-PASS verdict carries zero `findings` AND zero `criteria`, set `verdict_obtainable=false`'
gate_ops.py:295 sets `result["criteria"] = list(ctx.inputs.get("raw_criteria") or [])` immediately before `reconcile_verdict(result)` at gate_ops.py:297
Step 2 only says gate_ops 'inherits the marker by delegating to reconcile_verdict' and does not address that criteria is pre-populated from inputs on this path
findings.finding: The decision rule 'non-PASS verdict carries zero findings AND zero criteria => verdict_obtainable=false' can be defeated on the workflow close-gate path because gate_ops.completion_reconcile sets result['criteria'] from ctx.inputs['raw_criteria'] BEFORE it delegates to reconcile_verdict, so a genuine bare-FAIL verifier fault whose input carried a criteria manifest will have a non-empty result['criteria'] and NOT be marked a verifier fault.
findings.location: Implementation plan Step 2 (reconcile_verdict / gate_ops.completion_reconcile bullets); gate_ops.py:295-297
scenarios: Model returns a bare FAIL (no findings, no per-criterion records) during a workflow close where the ticket has a criteria manifest, so raw_criteria is non-empty
Any close-gate verifier fault where the framework injected criteria from inputs
findings.suggested_fix: Have reconcile_verdict decide verdict_obtainable from the model-emitted findings/criteria captured before any framework injection (e.g. read the raw agent output, or move the criteria-from-inputs assignment after reconcile_verdict), and state this ordering explicitly in Step 2.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct Root cause 1b: the prompt does not contain '<untrusted_ticket_context>' nor name show_ticket 'authoritative' at lines 26-28 — re-derive the actual prompt language (and re-verify the causal claim about why the model preferred the pinned snapshot) or cite the real text.
evidence: Plan: 'The prompt labels the context <untrusted_ticket_context> and names show_ticket authoritative (reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28)'
grep '<untrusted_ticket_context>' in src/rebar/llm/reviewers/completion_verifier.md → (no matches)

findings.finding: Root cause 1b asserts the verifier prompt 'labels the context <untrusted_ticket_context> and names show_ticket authoritative (reviewers/completion_verifier.md:26-28)'. A Read/Grep of the actual prompt refutes both: the literal string '<untrusted_ticket_context>' does not appear anywhere in the file (the label used is 'UNTRUSTED DATA', lines 30-35), and lines 26-28 only describe show_ticket as a read-only tool — nothing there names it 'authoritative' ('authoritative' appears only at lines 262 and 290, in unrelated state-machine/structured-output contexts). This is load-bearing: Root cause 1b's causal claim that 'the model correctly preferred the stale snapshot' because the prompt names show_ticket authoritative, and Step 3a's prompt-edit fix, both rest on prompt text that does not exist.
scenarios: An implementer reads the prompt to confirm the causal story and cannot find the cited language, casting doubt on the whole Root-cause-1b mechanism
Step 3a's prompt edit is authored against a mental model of prompt text that isn't there
